data.prompt:
You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: pic-e
Title: Pic rep lane E: close Pic representability, no new hypotheses
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
References: roadmap=AJC.jacobian,AJC.picrep; inbox=I-0838

Pic representability should close, and closing it is your objective — pick a roadmap item and make major progress on it, USING NO ADDITIONAL HYPOTHESIS (`rep` has 93 consumers and 0 producers; last round added 71 more consumers and the headline did not move). Your work must be directly usable by Pic representability and the other items, not local to your row. Be ambitious: don't scope down because something is large or missing from mathlib — building substrate and huge refactoring are licensed. Delete unfaithful roadmap items and create truer ones, but never a row another lane owns at HEAD. Collaborate with the other lanes; announce what you take before you start.

YOUR PEERS this round are pic-a, pic-b, pic-c, pic-d, pic-e, pic-f, pic-g, pic-h — eight provers, no reviewer. Four work Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (pic-a, pic-b, pic-e, pic-f) and four work Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild (pic-c, pic-d, pic-g, pic-h). With eight lanes on one ledger, announcing what you take BEFORE you start is what stops two lanes proving the same lemma — read the inbox for what the others announced, and say so if you are taking something already held.

This is a headless, one-shot session: advance the REAL objective, commit each
verified unit and any final edits, keep operational comments to the delta,
then write the skill's brief final report.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.
355

493	/-- **The pointed Picard theorem, with projectivity in place of `FiniteInAffine`.**
494	
495	Identical to `Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep` except in the last conjunct: it asks that the
496	representing scheme be **projective over the base**, which is the FGA/Kleiman conclusion,
497	rather than that finite subsets of it lie in affine opens, which is a consequence.
498	
499	Every remark in `PointedPicSharpRep`'s docstring about the *shape* still applies — the
500	uniformity in `K` is what lets §4 of `Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean` apply it at a
501	Galois level, and `IsSeparated` is still absent because it is free. What changes is only
502	that a lane discharging this owes a theorem someone has written down. -/
503	def PointedPicSharpRepProjective : Prop :=
504	  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
505	    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
506	      Scheme.HasRationalPoint E →

508	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy X) ∧

510	
511	/-- **The projective antecedent implies the elementary one.** Directly by §3, since the
512	base of the representing object is `Spec K`, which is affine.
513	
514	So §5's antecedent is at least as strong as §4's; whether it is *strictly* stronger is
515	not claimed here, and the converse is not proved — `FiniteInAffine` does not obviously

521	  intro K _ E _ _ _ hpt

523	  exact ⟨X, hrep, hlft, finiteInAffine_of_isProjective hproj⟩

544	/-- **The seam, verbatim, from the projective antecedent** — the statement of
545	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` character for character.
546	
547	Composing §5.2 with `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep`
548	(`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`). So the project's central `sorry` now follows by
549	`exact` from *projectivity* of the pointed Picard scheme, uniformly in the base field —

554	**AND ITS ANTECEDENT IS REFUTED AT THE INTENDED OBJECT — read §5.5 before consuming
555	this.** `PointedPicSharpRepProjective` demands projectivity of the scheme representing
556	the *whole* of `picSharp`, and §5.5 shows that forces `CompactSpace`, which the

565	theorem fgaPicardRepresentability_of_projective {k : Type u} [Field k]
566	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
567	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
568	    (H : PointedPicSharpRepProjective.{u}) :
569	    (∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
570	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
571	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom)
572	      ∧ (Scheme.HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
573	  fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep C (pointedPicSharpRep_of_projective H)

577	Landed as theorems rather than left as a caveat, because a caveat is what let the
578	overclaim through in the first place. A fresh-context audit of §5 found this; both
579	statements below were reproduced before the correction was accepted.

581	
582	/-- **Projectivity over a field forces a compact space.**
583	
584	`IsProjective → IsProper` is `Scheme.Hom.IsProjective.isProper`; mathlib derives
585	`QuasiCompact` from `UniversallyClosed` at `priority := 900`, and `Spec k` is compact, so

588	That file is where this chain was worked out, for `UniversallyClosed`. The point of
589	restating it for `IsProjective` is that §5's antecedent asks for the *projectivity*, so the
590	obstruction has to be visible from the hypothesis §5 actually carries. -/
591	theorem compactSpace_of_isProjective {k : Type u} [Field k]
592	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (h : X.hom.IsProjective) :
593	    CompactSpace X.left :=
594	  haveI := h.isProper
595	  compactSpace_of_universallyClosed X.hom
596	
597	/-- **A scheme with an infinite disjoint open cover is not projective over a field** —
598	the refutation of §5's antecedent, at scheme generality and with no Picard vocabulary.
599	
600	Composes `compactSpace_of_isProjective` with the pure-topology
601	`not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover` (`Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean`).
602	
603	**Why this refutes §5 and not §3 or §4.** The full relative Picard scheme is a disjoint
604	union of open pieces indexed by `deg ∈ ℤ` — that is the second clause of Kleiman §4
605	`th:main`(1), and it is what `HasPicScheme` bundles. An infinite family of pairwise
606	disjoint nonempty opens covering a space has no finite subcover, so `Pic_{C/k}` is not
607	quasi-compact and hence not projective over `k`. `PointedPicSharpRepProjective` asks for
608	exactly that projectivity, so it is false at its intended witness.
609	
610	Kleiman's `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of each **degree piece**. A repaired §5
611	would ask for that, piecewise, and would need degree-graded vocabulary this file does not
612	have; it is not attempted here, and pretending the gap is smaller than that is what the
613	retracted §5 docstring did. §3 and §4 are untouched: neither mentions the ambient Picard
614	scheme, and `finiteInAffine_curve` is about the curve, which *is* projective. -/
615	theorem not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover {k : Type u} [Field k]
616	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) {ι : Type v} [Infinite ι]
617	    (U : ι → Set X.left) (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) (hne : ∀ i, (U i).Nonempty)
618	    (hdisj : _root_.Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint U))
619	    (hcov : (Set.univ : Set X.left) ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) :
620	    ¬ X.hom.IsProjective := fun h =>
621	  not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover U hopen hne hdisj hcov
622	    (compactSpace_of_isProjective X h)

627	Kleiman's, and Kleiman's hypothesis is about the **degree pieces**: each `Pic^d_{C/k}` is
628	quasi-projective, and the ambient scheme is their disjoint union. So the repair is not a

632	deliberately does **not** do is define a "locally `FiniteInAffine`" predicate of the form

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtPointedReduction
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveMorphismBasic
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CurveProjectivity
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.AmbientPicNotProper

/-!
# Quasi-projectivity, as the vocabulary `FiniteInAffine` was standing in for

`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`) says every finite
subset of `X` lies in a single affine open.  It is the elementary, action-free form
of the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis that the whole finite-Galois-quotient engine runs
on, and up to now the project carried it **by hand**, with the same sentence
written in three places: *"it holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no
quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by
hand"* (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`,
`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).

This file removes the hand: it derives `FiniteInAffine` **from projectivity**, for
the project's own `Scheme.Hom.IsProjective`.  The chain is

  graded prime avoidance  ⟹  `FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜)`
                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine ℙ(n; S)`   (affine morphism descent)
                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine X` for `X` projective over `S`.

## What was actually missing, and it is one lemma

Of those three steps only the first has content, and it is **absent from mathlib
`v4.31`**: there is no *graded* prime avoidance.  Mathlib has
`Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite` — a homogeneous ideal not contained in the union
of finitely many primes is not contained in any one of them — but the element it
produces is an arbitrary element of the ideal, while
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen` demands `f ∈ 𝒜 m` with `0 < m`.
Getting a **homogeneous** avoiding element of **positive degree** is §1, and it is
where the grading is consumed.

The two descent steps are cheap and they are cheap for a reason worth recording:
`IsClosedImmersion → IsAffineHom` is a mathlib instance, and `IsAffineOpen.preimage`
turns an affine open of the target into an affine open of the source.  So
`FiniteInAffine` propagates **down** every affine morphism
(`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom`), and a closed immersion into `ℙ(n; S)` is
one.  This is the same shape as the already-landed
`Scheme.finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom`, generalised off the relative setting.

## What this does and does not buy

It does **not** discharge the `FiniteInAffine` conjunct of
`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep`.  That conjunct is about the **Picard scheme**, and
nothing in this project produces projectivity of a Picard scheme — that is
Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p`, an open obligation.  What changes is the *kind* of thing
that is open: the antecedent's last non-projection conjunct is now reducible to a
standard geometric hypothesis with a standard proof, rather than an elementary
condition invented here.  Stated as `Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isProjective` in §3.

It **does** discharge, unconditionally and for free, the orbit hypothesis of the
Galois-descent engine at every projective scheme

=== FiniteInAffine definition ===

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivFamilyZero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FGAPicRepresentability
8	
9	/-!
10	# The Abel map at the empty divisor
11	
12	`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` supplies the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily`. This
13	file spends it on the one place where having an inhabitant changes what can be
14	*checked* rather than merely stated: the **Abel map**
15	
16	  `A_{C/k} : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`,  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[I_D]`.
17	
18	`Scheme.PicScheme.abelMap_app_mk` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) states the
19	defining property `A([D]) = -[ker q]` for an arbitrary family. Before this file that
20	equation had **no instantiation**: `DivFamily` had no producer, so no value of the Abel
21	map was ever computed, and "the Abel map sends divisors to their line bundles" was a
22	statement about an empty domain.
23	
24	## What is proved
25	
26	`abelMap_zero`: `A([∅]) = 0`, i.e. the empty divisor goes to the **identity** of the
27	relative Picard group. Kleiman §3: `O(∅) = O`, so this is the normalisation an Abel map
28	must satisfy, and it is the first computed value of `abelMap` in the project.
29	
30	The proof is where the empty divisor's arithmetic shows up. `ker (0 : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0)` is
31	`O_{X_T}` (`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`, composed with
32	`Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso` because `DivFamily.q`'s source is stated as the
33	*pulled-back* unit). The zero of `PicSharp.relPresheaf` is *by definition* the class of
34	the unit line bundle (`Scheme.PicSharp.addCommGroup_via_tensorObj`), so the ideal class
35	is the group identity, and `neg_zero` finishes.
36	
37	## What this is not
38	
39	It is not a step of the seam: `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is untouched, and no
40	antecedent of it is witnessed. It also does **not** discharge
41	`IdentityComponent.ClassDegreePinned`'s acceptance test
42	(`classDegree_ne_zero_of_exists_pos_fiberDeg`), which needs a divisor family of
43	degree `d ≠ 0` — the empty divisor has degree `0`, so it is exactly the family that
44	test cannot use. That producer is still owed, and it needs a rational point.
45	
46	What it does buy: the Abel map's defining equation, and the degree ledger of
47	`Picard/DivDegree.lean`, now have a worked instance to be wrong about. `abelDeg_zero`
48	below records the same value through the degree-refined Abel map, which is the form the
49	campaign's D-cluster consumes.
50	-/
51	
52	set_option autoImplicit false
53	
54	universe u
55	
56	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry TopologicalSpace
57	
58	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
59	
60	namespace Scheme
61	
62	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
63	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
64	
65	/-- **The ideal sheaf of the empty divisor is the structure sheaf**, as a class in the
66	relative Picard group: `[I_∅] = [O] = 0`.
67	
68	`ker (0 : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0) ≅ O_{X_T}` by `kernelZeroIsoSource`, then
69	`Modules.pullbackUnitIso` identifies `DivFamily.q`'s pulled-back-unit source with the
70	structure sheaf, and the zero of `relPresheaf` *is* the unit class. -/
71	theorem PicSharp.kernelClass_divFamilyZero (T : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
72	    (Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
73	      (⟨kernel (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop).q,
74	        (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop).kerLocallyTrivial⟩ :
75	        LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom))
76	      = (0 : (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T) :=
77	  Quotient.sound (PicSharp.relPicRel_of_iso
78	    ⟨Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource ≪≫ Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso _⟩)
79	
80	variable [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
81	
82	/-- **THE ABEL MAP SENDS THE EMPTY DIVISOR TO THE IDENTITY**: `A([∅]) = 0`.
83	
84	`O(∅) = O` (Kleiman §3), the normalisation any Abel map must satisfy — and the **first
85	computed value of `abelMap` in this project**, since `DivFamily` had no inhabitant to
86	evaluate it at before `Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean`.
87	
88	Stated against `abelMapWitness`'s instance, i.e. via `abelMap_app_mk`, not under an
89	arbitrary `[HasAbelMap C]` binder — that class is a data slot inhabited by the constant
90	zero map, for which `abelMap_app_mk` provably fails (see its docstring, `I-0953`). Under
91	*that* inhabitant this equation would hold trivially and say nothing, which is exactly
92	why the instance matters here. -/
93	theorem PicScheme.abelMap_zero (T : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
94	    (PicScheme.abelMap C).app T
95	        (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop))
96	      = (0 : (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T) := by
97	  rw [PicScheme.abelMap_app_mk, PicSharp.kernelClass_divFamilyZero]
98	  exact neg_zero (G := ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T : Type _))
99	
100	/-- **The degree-refined Abel map at the empty divisor**, in the form the campaign's
101	D-cluster consumes: `A⁰([∅]) = 0`.
102	
103	`abelDeg C 0` is `divFunctorDegι ≫ abelMapWitness`, so this is `abelMap_zero` transported
104	along the degree-`0` inclusion; `abelDeg_app_mk` supplies the transport. -/
105	theorem PicScheme.abelDeg_zero (T : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
106	    (PicScheme.abelDeg C 0).app T (DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass C.hom T.unop)
107	      = (0 : (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T) := by
108	  rw [show (DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass C.hom T.unop) =
109	      ⟨Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop),
110	        DivFunctor.classHasFiberDeg_zeroClass C.hom T.unop⟩ from rfl,
111	    PicScheme.abelDeg_app_mk]
112	  exact PicScheme.abelMap_zero C T

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivDegree
7	
8	/-!
9	# The empty divisor: the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily`
10	
11	`Scheme.DivFamily π T` (`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`) is the carrier of the whole
12	divisor side of the Milne–Kollár campaign: `Scheme.DivFunctor`, its degree slices
13	`Scheme.DivFunctorDeg`, the Abel maps `abelDeg` / `abelMapWitness`, the flatness
14	inputs of `Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean`, and `IdentityComponent`'s
15	`ClassDegreePinned` acceptance test are all quantified over it. Until this file it
16	had **zero producers**, for any `π`, any base, and any test object including the
17	trivial one — measured with `exact?` and recorded in its own docstring. The
18	consequence recorded there: *every* statement quantified over a `DivFamily` was
19	"true but untested", with no instance to be wrong about.
20	
21	This file supplies the first inhabitant, unconditionally in `π : X ⟶ S` and
22	`T : Over S`: the **empty divisor** `D = ∅`, whose structure sheaf `O_D` is the
23	zero module and whose ideal is all of `O_{X_T}`.
24	
25	## Why the empty divisor satisfies the divisor condition
26	
27	The divisor condition of `DivFamily` is that the kernel ideal `I = ker q` be
28	*invertible* (`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`). For `q : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0` the kernel is
29	`O_{X_T}` itself (`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`), and the structure sheaf is
30	trivially locally trivial (`Scheme.PicSharp.isLocallyTrivial_unit`, restated here as
31	`isLocallyTrivial_unit'` because that one is `private`). So the invertible-ideal
32	condition — the field that makes `DivFamily` a divisor rather than an arbitrary
33	quotient — holds *for the reason it should*: `O_{X_T}/O_{X_T} = 0` cuts out the
34	empty subscheme, an effective divisor of degree zero.
35	
36	The three remaining fields are properties of the zero module, and the file proves
37	each rather than assuming it:
38	
39	* `isFinitePresentation` — the zero module is finitely presented. Mathlib has no
40	  instance for this (measured: `infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
41	  `(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so §1 builds the `QuasicoherentData`:
42	  the singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site
43	  (`coversTop_singleton_top`), the restriction functor preserves zero objects
44	  (`preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`, proved from `PresheafOfModules` extensionality
45	  because instance search for it times out), and a zero sheaf of modules has an
46	  *empty* presentation — no generators and no relations, both trivially finite.
47	* `flat` — flatness over the base. The section modules of a zero module are
48	  subsingletons, and a subsingleton module is flat.
49	* `properSupport` — the schematic support of the zero module is the subscheme cut
50	  out by the annihilator, which is `⊤`, so the support is **empty**
51	  (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.instIsEmptyCarrierCarrierCommRingCatSubschemeTop`) and any
52	  morphism out of it is proper via `IsProper.instOfIsFinite`. It is free here for that
53	  reason, and in particular with **no properness assumption on `π`**. (An earlier
54	  revision added "and it is a real hypothesis for a nonempty divisor". That half was
55	  never measured — nothing here or elsewhere in the project exhibits a divisor where
56	  `properSupport` fails or is expensive, and `DivFunctorDef.lean` says it is *automatic*
57	  when `π` is proper. Dropped rather than repaired: the free-here half is what this
58	  file establishes.)
59	
60	## What this does and does not buy
61	
62	**Does**: the divisor cluster is no longer vacuous. `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)` for
63	every `π` and `T`; `(DivFunctor π).obj (op T)` and `(DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T)`
64	are inhabited; `HasFiberDeg zero 0`; and the base-change action carries `zero` to
65	`zero` (`pullbackAlong_zero`), so the classes are a global section of `DivFunctor`
66	rather than a fibrewise accident. Every theorem in `DivDegree.lean` and
67	`DivPushforwardFlat.lean` now has a witness to be checked against.
68	
69	**Does not**: this closes no `sorry` and witnesses no antecedent of
70	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`. In particular it is *not* a step of D1′: the
71	campaign's D1′ wants divisor families of a **prescribed positive degree** `d`
72	arising from a very ample `O(1)`, which needs the projectivity input
73	(`AJC.picrep.projectivity`) and P5 uniform `H¹` vanishing. What the empty divisor
74	does for that programme is remove the possibility that the target type is
75	uninhabited — a question that had to be settled before any positive-degree producer
76	could be believed, and which no lane had settled in either direction.
77	
78	**One caveat, stated because it is the natural over-reading.** The degree-zero slice
79	being inhabited does *not* make `DivFunctorDeg π 0` representable by the terminal
80	object `Over.mk (𝟙 S)`. That would need the slice to be a *singleton* at every test
81	object, and this file proves only the `Nonempty` half. The missing half is
82	`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — i.e. that the empty divisor is the
83	*only* relative divisor of degree `0`. That is the expected statement (a degree-`0`
84	effective divisor on a fibre of a relative curve is empty), but it is a fact about
85	`fiberDeg`, not a formality: `fiberDeg` is a `finrank` with a junk value at
86	infinite dimension. Neither direction is proved here.
87	
88	**Corrected, and the correction is the useful part** (fresh-context audit of this file,
89	2026-07-30). An earlier revision of this paragraph said "no lane holds it". That is
90	FALSE: the analogous `Subsingleton` *is* landed, hours earlier, on the **sibling**
91	project's carrier — `instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero`
92	(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean`) and, over an arbitrary test ring,
93	`instSubsingletonDivFamZarZeroGeneral` plus a full `RepresentableBy` producer
94	(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroRep.lean`).
95	
96	What survives, for a **sharper** reason than the carrier mismatch: their proof is not
97	portable because it never passes through a `finrank` at all. It runs on `IsCertified`
98	and `rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton` over `Away` localisations of section rings,
99	machinery that exists only on the Zariski-certified carrier `DivFamZar : Type u`. AJC's
100	`fiberDeg` is a `Module.finrank` of fibre sections. So the honest statement is: nobody
101	holds it *for `Scheme.DivFamily`*, and the sibling's landed route does not transport.
102	Their success is also evidence *against* this paragraph's own framing — it shows
103	degree-zero uniqueness can be reached without any finiteness-of-sections argument on a
104	suitable carrier, so "needs finiteness of the fibre sections" is a claim about AJC's
105	chosen `fiberDeg`, not about the mathematics. The row `AJC.picrep.divzero` records it as
106	the open question this file leaves.
107	
108	## Main declarations
109	
110	* `Scheme.DivFamily.zero π T` — the empty divisor family.
111	* `Scheme.DivFamily.instNonempty` — `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)`, as an instance.
112	* `Scheme.DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero` — base change carries `zero` to `zero`.
113	* `Scheme.DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero` / `hasFiberDeg_zero` — the empty divisor has
114	  fibre degree `0` at every point.
115	* `Scheme.DivFunctor.zeroClass` / `Scheme.DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass` — the resulting
116	  inhabitants of the functor and of its degree-`0` slice, with
117	  `Scheme.DivFunctor.map_zeroClass` making the first a global section.
118	* `Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_isZero` — reusable: a zero sheaf of
119	  modules on any scheme is finitely presented. Absent from Mathlib.
120	* `Scheme.Modules.coversTop_singleton_top`,
121	  `Scheme.Modules.preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`,
122	  `Scheme.Modules.isZero_free_pempty` — the other reusable bricks §1 needed.
123	
124	Every declaration here is `sorry`-free and axiom-clean
125	(`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`), measured against
126	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` reporting `sorryAx` in the same probe file with the
127	oleans rebuilt first.
128	
129	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:red`/`df:div`, Ex. `ex:DivC`
130	(arXiv:math/0504020).
131	-/
132	
133	set_option autoImplicit false
134	
135	universe u
136	
137	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry ZeroObject TopologicalSpace
138	
139	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
140	
141	/-! ## §1. A zero sheaf of modules is finitely presented
142	
143	Mathlib carries no instance for this (`infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
144	`(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so the `QuasicoherentData` is built by
145	hand: one cover member `⊤`, no generators, no relations. -/
146	
147	namespace Scheme.Modules
148	
149	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}}
150	
151	/-- **The singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site.**
152	
153	The one covering datum every "global" presentation needs, and the reason a *global*
154	presentation of a sheaf of modules on `Y` is already a `QuasicoherentData`: the sieve
155	`Sieve.ofObjects (fun _ => ⊤) V` is the top sieve at every open `V`, because
156	`V ≤ ⊤` supplies the required arrow. -/
157	theorem coversTop_singleton_top :
158	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (Y : TopCat)).CoversTop
159	      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) := by
160	  intro V
161	  have h : Sieve.ofObjects
162	      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) V = ⊤ := by
163	    ext W _
164	    simp only [Sieve.top_apply, iff_true]
165	    exact ⟨PUnit.unit, ⟨homOfLE le_top⟩⟩
166	  rw [h]
167	  exact GrothendieckTopology.top_mem _ _
168	
169	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- slice-site sheafification blow-up
170	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
171	/-- **The restriction functor to an open preserves zero morphisms.**
172	
173	`SheafOfModules.overFunctor` is `SheafOfModules.pushforward (𝟙 _)`, which acts as the
174	identity on section groups, so the statement is `rfl` componentwise. It is proved
175	rather than synthesized because instance search for
176	`(overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms` exhausts its heartbeat budget
177	(measured: `deterministic timeout at typeclass, 20000 heartbeats`) — the
178	sheafification/slice-site instances it unfolds are the same blow-up
179	`Scheme.Modules.presentationPullbackιOfQuasicoherentData` documents. -/
180	theorem preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat)) :
181	    (SheafOfModules.overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms := by
182	  constructor
183	  intro _ _
184	  apply SheafOfModules.hom_ext
185	  apply PresheafOfModules.hom_ext
186	  intro _
187	  rfl
188	
189	/-- **The empty generating sections of a zero sheaf of modules.**
190	
191	No generators at all: the structure map `free PEmpty ⟶ M` is epi because *every*
192	morphism into a zero object is, so there is nothing to generate. Stated for a general
193	sheaf of rings on the opens site so that both `M` and its restrictions `M.over U`
194	can use it. -/
195	def zeroGeneratingSections
196	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
197	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
198	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
199	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
200	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : M.GeneratingSections where
201	  I := PEmpty.{u+1}
202	  s j := PEmpty.elim j
203	  epi := ⟨fun {_} g h _ => hM.eq_of_src g h⟩
204	
205	instance zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType
206	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
207	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
208	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
209	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
210	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) :
211	    (zeroGeneratingSections hM).IsFiniteType where
212	  finite := (inferInstance : Finite PEmpty.{u+1})
213	
214	/-- **`free PEmpty` is an initial, hence zero, sheaf of modules.**
215	
216	There is exactly one morphism out of it into any target — `freeHomEquiv` turns a
217	morphism `free PEmpty ⟶ Z` into a family of sections indexed by `PEmpty`, of which
218	there is one — so it is initial, and an initial object in a category with zero
219	morphisms is a zero object. -/
220	theorem isZero_free_pempty
221	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
222	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
223	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
224	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})] :
225	    IsZero (SheafOfModules.free (R := R) PEmpty.{u+1}) :=
226	  IsInitial.isZero <|
227	    IsInitial.ofUnique (h := fun Z =>
228	      ⟨⟨(SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv Z).symm (fun j => PEmpty.elim j)⟩,
229	        fun _ => (SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv Z).injective (funext fun j => PEmpty.elim j)⟩)
230	
231	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules has an empty presentation** — no generators and no
232	relations.
233	
234	The relations live in `kernel (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π`, whose source
235	`free PEmpty` is itself a zero object (`isZero_free_pempty`), so the kernel is zero
236	too and the empty family generates it for the same reason. -/
237	theorem isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections
238	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
239	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
240	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
241	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
242	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) :
243	    IsZero (kernel (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π) :=
244	  haveI : Mono (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π := isZero_free_pempty.mono _
245	  isZero_kernel_of_mono _
246	
247	noncomputable def zeroPresentation
248	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
249	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
250	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
251	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
252	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : M.Presentation where
253	  generators := zeroGeneratingSections hM
254	  relations := zeroGeneratingSections (isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections hM)
255	
256	instance zeroPresentation_isFinite
257	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
258	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
259	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
260	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
261	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : (zeroPresentation hM).IsFinite where
262	  isFiniteType_generators := zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType hM
263	  isFiniteType_relations :=
264	    zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType (isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections hM)
265	
266	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- slice-site sheafification blow-up
267	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
268	/-- **The quasi-coherence datum of a zero sheaf of modules**: the singleton cover
269	`{⊤}`, with the empty presentation on it.
270	
271	The restriction `M.over ⊤` of a zero module is zero
272	(`preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor` plus `Functor.map_isZero`), so
273	`zeroPresentation` applies on the cover member. -/
274	theorem isZero_over_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M)
275	    (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat)) : IsZero (M.over U) :=
276	  haveI := preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor (Y := Y) U
277	  Functor.map_isZero (SheafOfModules.overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U) hM
278	
279	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- slice-site `Over top` instances
280	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
281	noncomputable def zeroQuasicoherentData {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
282	    M.QuasicoherentData where
283	  I := PUnit.{u+1}
284	  X _ := (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))
285	  coversTop := coversTop_singleton_top
286	  presentation _ := zeroPresentation (isZero_over_of_isZero hM _)
287	
288	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- as `zeroQuasicoherentData` above
289	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
290	instance zeroQuasicoherentData_isFinitePresentation {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
291	    (zeroQuasicoherentData hM).IsFinitePresentation where
292	  isFinite_presentation _ := zeroPresentation_isFinite (isZero_over_of_isZero hM _)
293	
294	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- `shrink` re-enters slice synthesis
295	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
296	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules on a scheme is finitely presented.**
297	
298	Absent from Mathlib: measured, `infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
299	`(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`. This is the field of `Scheme.DivFamily` that
300	had no route at `F = 0`, and it is why the empty divisor needed §1 rather than one
301	line. Everything else about the empty divisor is a one-lemma citation. -/
302	theorem isFinitePresentation_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
303	    M.IsFinitePresentation where
304	  exists_quasicoherentData :=
305	    ⟨(zeroQuasicoherentData hM).shrink,
306	      { isFinite_presentation := fun _ =>
307	          zeroPresentation_isFinite (isZero_over_of_isZero hM _) }⟩
308	
309	/-! ## §2. Flatness and proper support of a zero sheaf of modules -/
310	
311	/-- **The sections of a zero sheaf of modules over any open form a subsingleton.**
312	
313	`Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` is additive, so it carries `M` to a zero presheaf of
314	abelian groups, whose value at `V` is a zero object of `Ab` and hence a
315	subsingleton. -/
316	theorem subsingleton_sections_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M)
317	    (V : Y.Opens) : Subsingleton Γ(M, V) :=
318	  AddCommGrpCat.subsingleton_of_isZero
319	    ((Functor.map_isZero (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf Y) hM).obj _)
320	
321	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules is flat over any base morphism**, with no hypothesis on
322	the morphism at all.
323	
324	`CoherentSheafFlat` asks each section module `Γ(M, V)` to be flat over `Γ(S, U)`. The
325	section modules are subsingletons (`subsingleton_sections_of_isZero`), and a
326	subsingleton module is flat. -/
327	theorem coherentSheafFlat_of_isZero {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ S') {M : Y.Modules}
328	    (hM : IsZero M) : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat g M := by
329	  intro U _ V _ e
330	  letI : Module Γ(S', U) Γ(M, V) := Module.compHom _ (g.appLE U V e).hom
331	  haveI := subsingleton_sections_of_isZero hM V
332	  exact inferInstance
333	
334	/-- **The annihilator ideal sheaf of a zero sheaf of modules is `⊤`.**
335	
336	Each affine-local annihilator is the whole ring (`Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff` at a
337	subsingleton module), and `ofIdeals` of the constant-`⊤` family is `⊤` because `⊤` is
338	itself an ideal sheaf below it. -/
339	theorem annihilator_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
340	    Scheme.Modules.annihilator M = ⊤ :=
341	  top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup (by
342	    intro U
343	    haveI := subsingleton_sections_of_isZero hM U.1
344	    exact le_of_eq (Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff.mpr inferInstance).symm))
345	
346	/-- **The schematic support of a zero sheaf of modules is empty.**
347	
348	Its annihilator is `⊤`, and the subscheme cut out by the unit ideal sheaf has empty
349	carrier. -/
350	theorem isEmpty_schematicSupport_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
351	    IsEmpty (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport M) := by
352	  rw [Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport, annihilator_of_isZero hM]
353	  infer_instance
354	
355	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules has proper support over any base**, unconditionally.
356	
357	The support is empty, and a morphism out of an empty scheme is finite, hence proper.
358	This is the field of `DivFamily` that is a *real* hypothesis for a nonempty divisor —
359	properness of `D → T` — and it is free for the empty one, with **no** properness
360	assumption on the ambient morphism. -/
361	theorem hasProperSupport_of_isZero {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ S') {M : Y.Modules}
362	    (hM : IsZero M) : Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport g M := by
363	  haveI := isEmpty_schematicSupport_of_isZero hM
364	  exact IsProper.instOfIsFinite _
365	
366	end Scheme.Modules
367	
368	/-! ## §3. The empty divisor -/
369	
370	namespace Scheme
371	
372	variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ S) (T : Over S)
373	
374	/-- **The structure sheaf is locally trivial of rank one.**
375	
376	`Scheme.PicSharp.isLocallyTrivial_unit` is `private`, so it is restated here rather
377	than reused: on any affine open the identity is the required trivialisation. -/
378	theorem isLocallyTrivial_unit' {Y : Scheme.{u}} :
379	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf) := by
380	  intro x
381	  obtain ⟨W, hW_aff, hxW, -⟩ :=
382	    exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (X := Y) (x := x) (U := ⊤)
383	      (show x ∈ (⊤ : Y.Opens) from trivial)
384	  exact ⟨W, hxW, hW_aff,
385	    ⟨(Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback W.ι).app _ ≪≫ Modules.pullbackUnitIso W.ι⟩⟩
386	
387	/-- **THE EMPTY DIVISOR**, and with it the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily` for
388	any `π : X ⟶ S` and any test object `T`.
389	
390	`F = 0`, `q = 0`. The kernel ideal is then all of `O_{X_T}` — via
391	`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`, since the source of `q` is the pulled-back unit — which
392	is invertible, so the *divisor condition* holds for the geometric reason it should:
393	`O_{X_T}/O_{X_T} = 0` cuts out `D = ∅`, an effective relative divisor.
394	
395	No hypothesis on `π`: not proper, not smooth, not even separated. Compare the general
396	case, where `properSupport` and `flat` are substantive conditions. -/
397	noncomputable def DivFamily.zero : DivFamily π T where
398	  F := 0
399	  isFinitePresentation := Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_isZero (isZero_zero _)
400	  flat := Modules.coherentSheafFlat_of_isZero _ (isZero_zero _)
401	  properSupport := Modules.hasProperSupport_of_isZero _ (isZero_zero _)
402	  q := 0
403	  epi := (isZero_zero _).epi _
404	  kerLocallyTrivial :=
405	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
406	      (Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource (X := (Scheme.Modules.pullback
407	        (Limits.pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))
408	        (Y := (0 : (Limits.pullback π T.hom).Modules))).symm
409	      (LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
410	        (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.fst π T.hom)).symm
411	        isLocallyTrivial_unit')
412	
413	instance DivFamily.instNonempty : Nonempty (DivFamily π T) :=
414	  ⟨DivFamily.zero π T⟩
415	
416	/-! ## §4. Base change, fibre degree, and the degree-zero slice
417	
418	The empty divisor is not just a fibrewise accident: base change carries it to the
419	empty divisor of the new test object, so its classes assemble into a **global section**
420	of `DivFunctor`, and its fibre degree is `0` at every point of every base. -/
421	
422	/-- **The pulled-back empty divisor is the empty divisor**, up to the divisor
423	equivalence — both `F`-sheaves are zero and any two morphisms into a zero object
424	agree.
425	
426	This is what makes `zeroClass` below a genuine global section of `DivFunctor` rather
427	than an unrelated choice at each test object. -/
428	theorem DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero {T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
429	    ((DivFamily.zero π T).pullbackAlong ψ).Rel (DivFamily.zero π T') :=
430	  ⟨(Functor.map_isZero (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ))
431	      (isZero_zero _)).iso (isZero_zero _),
432	    (isZero_zero _).eq_of_tgt _ _⟩
433	
434	/-- **The fibre of the empty divisor is zero** — `fiberModule` is a module pullback,
435	which is additive. -/
436	theorem DivFamily.isZero_fiberModule_zero (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
437	    IsZero ((Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (DivFamily.zero π T).F) :=
438	  Functor.map_isZero _ (isZero_zero _)
439	
440	/-- **The empty divisor has fibre degree `0`**, at every point of every base.
441	
442	`deg ∅ = dim_{κ(t)} Γ(∅, O_∅) = 0`: the fibre is the zero module, its global sections
443	are a subsingleton, and `finrank` of a subsingleton is `0`. -/
444	theorem DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
445	    (DivFamily.zero π T).fiberDeg t = 0 := by
446	  letI := (Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
447	    ((Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (DivFamily.zero π T).F)
448	  haveI : Subsingleton
449	      Γ((Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (DivFamily.zero π T).F, ⊤) :=
450	    Modules.subsingleton_sections_of_isZero (DivFamily.isZero_fiberModule_zero π T t) _
451	  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
452	
453	/-- **The empty divisor has constant fibre degree `0`** — `HasFiberDeg zero 0`, the
454	predicate the degree-`d` subfunctor `DivFunctorDeg` is cut out by. -/
455	theorem DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_zero : (DivFamily.zero π T).HasFiberDeg 0 :=
456	  fun t => DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero π T t
457	
458	/-- **The class of the empty divisor** in `Div_{X/S}(T)`: the first inhabitant of the
459	relative-divisor functor's value at any test object. -/
460	noncomputable def DivFunctor.zeroClass : (DivFunctor π).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
461	  Quotient.mk _ (DivFamily.zero π T)
462	
463	instance DivFunctor.instNonemptyObj : Nonempty ((DivFunctor π).obj (Opposite.op T)) :=
464	  ⟨DivFunctor.zeroClass π T⟩
465	
466	/-- **`DivFunctor` carries the zero class to the zero class**, i.e. `zeroClass` is a
467	*global section* of `Div_{X/S}` — a compatible family over all test objects, not a
468	choice per object. -/
469	theorem DivFunctor.map_zeroClass {T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
470	    (DivFunctor π).map ψ.op (DivFunctor.zeroClass π T) = DivFunctor.zeroClass π T' :=
471	  Quotient.sound (DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero π T ψ)
472	
473	/-- **The empty divisor's class has degree `0`**, in the class-level predicate the
474	degree slices use. -/
475	theorem DivFunctor.classHasFiberDeg_zeroClass :
476	    DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg (π := π) 0 (DivFunctor.zeroClass π T) :=
477	  DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_zero π T
478	
479	/-- **The degree-`0` slice `Div⁰_{X/S}(T)` is inhabited**, for every `π` and every
480	test object.
481	
482	This is the statement that turns the whole degree apparatus of `Picard/DivDegree.lean`
483	from vacuous into tested. Note what it is *not*: an identification of the slice with a
484	point. See the file docstring — singleton-ness at every test object is what
485	representability by the terminal object would need, and that is open. -/
486	noncomputable def DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass : (DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
487	  ⟨DivFunctor.zeroClass π T, DivFunctor.classHasFiberDeg_zeroClass π T⟩
488	
489	instance DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero :
490	    Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (Opposite.op T)) :=
491	  ⟨DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass π T⟩
492	
493	end Scheme
494	
495	end AlgebraicGeometry

12	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
13	
14	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
15	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
16	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
17	
18	The relative Picard functor is
19	
20	```
21	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
22	```
23	
24	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
25	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
26	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
27	against it is a natural bijection
28	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
29	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
30	
31	## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)
32	
33	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
34	that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
35	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
36	hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
37	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
38	sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
39	localised at `Spec k`.
40	
41	Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
42	`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
43	general field, so an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a
44	**false** statement, not merely an unproved one.
45	
46	**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`), by reading the source. The
47	conclusion above is right; the reason previously given for it was not.** This
48	paragraph used to say `picSharp` "is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
49	L1292–L1302)". Those lines
50	(`references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex`, the full paper) say
51	something else: "The **absolute** Picard functor `Pic_X` is never a separated
52	presheaf in the Zariski topology", proved with the `ℙ¹_X`/`O(1)` argument. That
53	is about `Pic_X`, **not** about the relative `Pic_{X/S} = picSharp`, which is
54	*defined* by quotienting out `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. What
55	Kleiman actually asserts about the relative functor is weaker (L1330): "Since
56	`Pic_{X/S}` is not *a priori* a sheaf, it is remarkable that it is representable
57	so often in practice." Not-a-priori is not never — indeed L1600–L1605 proves
58	`Pic_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever `f` has a section.
59	
60	**The witness, and it satisfies exactly this file's binders.** Kleiman
61	L5105–L5108 (repeated L5126–L5129): take `X : u² + v² + w² = 0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, a
62	smooth plane conic — hence smooth, proper, and geometrically integral, since
63	`X_ℂ ≅ ℙ¹_ℂ` — over a field where it has **no** rational point. `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}`
64	is representable by §4 `th:main`, the two functors differ (Exercise `ex:Pfs`),
65	and Kleiman concludes `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable.
66	
67	**That last step is now a Lean theorem rather than a quotation**, which is the
68	right state for something this load-bearing:
69	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
70	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`, `ajc-p1`) derives *from* `¬ IsIso
71	(picEtComparison C)` that **no** scheme represents `picSharp C` — the existential
72	of clause (1), not merely the pinned `PicScheme C`. No topology and no sheaf step
73	enter. So the falsity of the `picSharp` analogue of clause (1) is reduced to the
74	single residue that the comparison really does fail for that conic (via
75	`φ^* O(1)` and `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ`), which is where Kleiman's own argument lives and
76	is not yet formalised.
77	
78	**Do not route this through a Zariski-sheaf claim** (corrected again the same
79	day, after `work-reviewer` refuted the first repair — see `I-0970`). It is
80	tempting to argue "representable ⟹ Zariski sheaf, and `picSharp` is not one";
81	the second half is *not* what the sources say. `ex:Pfs` compares
82	`Pic_{(X/ℝ)zar}` with `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` — both already sheaves — so it witnesses
83	`zar ≠ ét`, not a failure of Zariski descent for the unsheafified functor. And
84	Kleiman `th:cmp` part 1 (L1391–L1393) proves `Pic_{X/S} ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}`
85	whenever `O_S ≅ f_* O_X` holds universally, which is automatic on these binders —
86	i.e. `picSharp` *is* Zariski-separated here, and any failure could only be
87	gluing. The non-representability above needs no sheaf step at all, so take it
88	directly. Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5** repairs it only under a
89	**section**: given one (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic for our
90	proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparisons
91	
92	```
93	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
94	```
95	
96	are bijective. That conditional route survives here as
97	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint` and `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`,
98	both clearly labelled as **strictly weaker than the challenge**. They are not
99	the headline and must not be reported as progress toward it. (Earlier revisions
100	of this file named a class `PicEtComparisonIso` in these four places; no such
101	declaration exists or ever landed — the comparison is supplied by the theorem
102	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, which is clause (2) of
103	`fgaPicardRepresentability` applied to the section. Corrected 2026-07-29.)

683	/-! ## §7. `FiniteInAffine` is closed under coproducts — the repair of §5's refutation
684	
685	`§5.5` shows the antecedent `PointedPicSharpRepProjective` — projectivity of the scheme
686	representing the *whole* of `picSharp` — is FALSE at its intended object, because
687	`Pic_{C/k} = ∐_{d ∈ ℤ} Pic^d` is a countable disjoint union and projectivity of it would
688	force `CompactSpace` (`compactSpace_of_isProjective`), which `Pic_{C/k}` is not
689	(`not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`).  The mathematically correct
690	statement is that the *pieces* `Pic^d` are projective and the Picard scheme is their
691	coproduct.
692	
693	`FiniteInAffine`, unlike `IsProjective` or `CompactSpace`, **is** closed under such
694	coproducts: a finite set meets only finitely many components, each hit in an affine open,
695	and finitely many disjoint affine opens have an affine `iSup`
696	(`IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint`).  So this section turns the refuted globally-projective
697	antecedent into the true degree-graded one — `FiniteInAffine` of the ambient Picard
698	scheme follows from projectivity of each degree piece, which is exactly the conjunct
699	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep` asks and the shape the Milne–Kollár degree assembly (`G4`)
700	produces.
701	
702	Everything here is about coproducts of arbitrary schemes and carries **no** hypothesis
703	about the curve; nothing closes the seam.  It is the substrate the earlier sections said
704	was missing ("degree-invariance of the semilinear action, together with the degree-graded
705	decomposition of `PicSchemeEt`" — the second half). -/

743	        (Scheme.Hom.image_le_opensRange _ _) (disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι g i j hij)
